edition: Based on the California Driver's Handbook, DL 600 English (rev. 6/2025), the current edition on dmv.ca.gov as checked October 2026

exam.rules: Everyone applying for a first California Class C license (an instruction permit) takes a multiple-choice knowledge test on the California Driver's Handbook at a DMV office, along with a vision test. DMV says the passing score is 80%. Adults (18 and older) get 36 questions and need 30 correct. Applicants under 18 get 46 questions and may miss no more than 8 (38 correct). Each question has three answer choices. Road-sign questions are mixed in with the other questions, not scored as a separate section. You get three attempts per application before you must reapply, and minors must wait 7 days (not counting the day of the failure) to retake a failed test. In-office tests must be started before 4:30 p.m. Testing aids such as the handbook or a phone are not allowed. Drivers renewing a license may be offered a no-fail eLearning course instead; first-time applicants may not use it.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to apply for a California provisional instruction permit?
questions.explain: Applicants under 18 must be at least 15½ years old to apply for an instruction permit.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Applying For An Instruction Permit'

questions.q: A driver under 18 must hold an instruction permit for at least how long before taking the behind-the-wheel drive test?
questions.explain: Minors must have held a permit for at least 6 months (or turn 18) before scheduling the drive test.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Applying For A Driver's License'

questions.q: How much supervised practice driving must a driver under 18 complete before getting a license?
questions.explain: Minors must log at least 50 hours of practice, 10 of them at night, with a licensed driver who is at least 25.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Applying For A Driver's License'

questions.q: A 16-year-old permit holder wants to practice with a licensed adult who is not a parent, guardian or instructor. How old must that driver be?
questions.explain: Minors with a permit must practice with a California-licensed driver who is at least 25 years old (or a parent, guardian or instructor).
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Applying For A Driver's License'

questions.q: An adult (18 or older) with an instruction permit may practice driving with a California-licensed driver who is at least:
questions.explain: Adult permit holders may practice with a California-licensed driver who is at least 18; the 25-year minimum applies to minors.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Applying For A Driver's License'

questions.q: What is the minimum age to get a provisional driver's license in California?
questions.explain: Applicants under 18 must be at least 16 years old to be issued a driver's license.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Applying For A Driver's License'

questions.q: During the first 12 months with a provisional license, you may not drive between:
questions.explain: Provisional drivers cannot drive from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. during the first year unless an exception applies.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Minor's Restrictions and Exceptions'

questions.q: During the first year with a provisional license, you may not carry passengers under what age unless an approved adult rides with you?
questions.explain: Provisional drivers may not transport passengers under 20 unless a parent, guardian or licensed driver 25 or older is in the vehicle.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Minor's Restrictions and Exceptions'

questions.q: A provisional driver needs to drive to work during restricted hours. What must they carry?
options: A note signed by any adult
A note signed by their employer confirming the employment
questions.explain: The work exception requires a note signed by the employer confirming employment.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Minor's Restrictions and Exceptions'

questions.q: When can a minor begin using a newly issued instruction permit to drive?
options: Once behind-the-wheel training has started with an instructor who validates the permit
Immediately after passing the knowledge test
questions.explain: A minor's permit is not valid for driving until they begin driver training and the instructor validates it.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 2, 'Applying For An Instruction Permit'

questions.q: How many attempts do you get to pass the knowledge test before you must reapply?
questions.explain: Applicants get three tries at the knowledge test before having to reapply.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 3, 'Driver's License Tests'

questions.q: If a minor fails the knowledge test, how long must they wait to retake it?
options: 7 days, not counting the day of the failure
questions.explain: Minors must wait seven days (excluding the failure day) before retaking a failed knowledge test.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 3, 'Driver's License Tests'

questions.q: If a minor fails the behind-the-wheel drive test, how long must they wait before retaking it?
options: 14 days, not counting the day of the failure
questions.explain: Minors must wait 14 days (excluding the failure day) before retaking a failed drive test.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 3, 'On the day of your behind-the-wheel test'

questions.q: After you move, how soon must you notify the DMV of your new address?
questions.explain: You must report a change of address to the DMV within ten days.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 4, 'Changing, Replacing, and Renewing Your Driver's License'

questions.q: When you sell a vehicle, you must notify the DMV within:
questions.explain: A Notice of Transfer and Release of Liability must be submitted within five days of selling a vehicle.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 11, 'Vehicle Registration Requirements'

questions.q: You become a California resident with an out-of-state vehicle. How long do you have to register it here?
questions.explain: Vehicles must be registered within 20 days of becoming a resident or taking a job in California.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 11, 'Vehicle Registration Requirements'

questions.q: For an adult, what is the lowest number of points within 12 months that can lead to suspension as a negligent driver?
questions.explain: An adult may be suspended for 4 points in 12 months, 6 in 24 months, or 8 in 36 months.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Points on Your Driver's Record'

questions.q: Which point total can lead to suspension of an adult driver's license?
questions.explain: Negligent-operator thresholds are 4 points/12 months, 6 points/24 months and 8 points/36 months.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Points on Your Driver's Record'

questions.q: A provisional driver has two at-fault collisions or traffic convictions in the first year. What happens?
options: Their license is revoked for 2 years
They must retake only the vision test
They cannot drive for 30 days unless accompanied by a licensed adult at least 25
questions.explain: Two at-fault collisions or convictions bring a 30-day restriction requiring a licensed adult 25+ in the car.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Maintaining Your Minor's (Provisional) Driver's License'

questions.q: A provisional driver accumulates three at-fault collisions or traffic convictions. What is the result?
options: A 6-month suspension and 1 year of probation
questions.explain: Three at-fault collisions or convictions lead to a six-month suspension followed by one year of probation.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Maintaining Your Minor's (Provisional) Driver's License'

questions.q: A provisional driver is suspended at 17 and turns 18 during the suspension. What happens?
options: The suspension converts to a warning
The suspension ends on the 18th birthday
The suspension continues; turning 18 does not end it
questions.explain: Turning 18 does not erase existing restrictions, suspensions or probation.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Maintaining Your Minor's (Provisional) Driver's License'

questions.q: A judge offers traffic violator school for a one-point violation. How often may you use this option?
options: As often as the judge allows
questions.explain: Traffic violator school for a one-point ticket can be used once in any 18-month period.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Violator School' / 'Suspension or Revocation'

questions.q: If you sign a traffic ticket and then fail to appear in court:
options: Nothing happens if you pay later
Your car is automatically registered as stolen
The DMV may suspend your driving privilege until you appear
questions.explain: A failure to appear goes on your record and the DMV may suspend your driving privilege until you appear.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Points on Your Driver's Record'

questions.q: When stopped by law enforcement, the driver must produce:
options: A driver's license, proof of insurance, and vehicle registration
questions.explain: Drivers must show their license, proof of insurance and registration on request.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Law Enforcement Stops'

questions.q: If an unlicensed person is caught driving your vehicle, the vehicle may be impounded for:
questions.explain: A vehicle driven by an unlicensed person may be impounded for 30 days.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Evading Law Enforcement'

questions.q: What must you do at this sign?
options: Slow down and proceed without stopping if the way is clear
Come to a full stop at the limit line or before the crosswalk, then go when it is safe
Stop only if other vehicles are present
questions.explain: A STOP sign requires a complete stop at the limit line, before the crosswalk, or before the intersection, then checking all directions.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign require you to do?
options: Slow down and be ready to stop to let traffic or pedestrians go first
Proceed; other drivers must yield to you
Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
questions.explain: A YIELD sign means slow down and be prepared to stop for any vehicle, bicyclist or pedestrian before continuing.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not enter the road or ramp where it is posted
questions.explain: This regulatory sign tells you not to enter the roadway or ramp where it is posted.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: You see this sign after entering a roadway. What should you do?
options: Continue carefully in the right lane
Speed up to reach the next exit
Stop in your lane and wait for help
You are going against traffic; safely back out or turn around
questions.explain: WRONG WAY means you are driving against traffic; when safe, back out or turn around.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign prohibit?
questions.explain: A red circle with a slash over a U-shaped arrow prohibits U-turns.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Left turns allowed only on green
questions.explain: The red circle and slash over a left arrow means no left turn.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: The red circle and slash over a right arrow means no right turn.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: At a red light where this sign is posted, you must:
options: Turn only if no pedestrians are present
Stop, then turn right when clear
Wait for a green light before turning
questions.explain: A NO TURN ON RED sign removes the usual permission to turn right on red after stopping.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Right Turns'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Turn in the direction of the arrow immediately
Traffic on this road moves only in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: A ONE WAY sign shows the only permitted direction of travel.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Stop only if a gate is down
Look, listen, slow down and be prepared to stop for trains
questions.explain: This marks a railroad crossing: look, listen, slow down, be ready to stop and let trains pass.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: This round yellow sign warns that you are:
questions.explain: A round yellow sign with an X and RR warns of a railroad crossing ahead.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: A five-sided (pentagon) sign means:
questions.explain: Five-sided signs mark school areas: drive slowly and stop for children in the crosswalk.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign?
options: Use the next lane to pass slower vehicles
Slow down and watch for children; stop for any in the crosswalk
Speed up to clear the area quickly
questions.explain: This sign marks a school area; drive slowly and stop for children crossing.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does a diamond-shaped sign usually indicate?
options: A service such as food or fuel
A warning about road conditions or hazards ahead
questions.explain: Diamond-shaped signs warn of specific road conditions and dangers ahead.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
questions.explain: This warning sign alerts you to a place where pedestrians may cross.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road is slippery when wet
questions.explain: This warns that the pavement becomes slippery when wet; slow down in rain.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: A lane is closed to the right
questions.explain: This sign shows another lane of traffic joining from the right; be ready to adjust speed and position.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: A new lane is added on the left
The right lane ends ahead; be ready to merge left
questions.explain: A lane-ends sign warns that a lane is ending and traffic must merge.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The divided highway ends; expect two-way traffic
questions.explain: This warns that the median ends and opposing traffic will no longer be separated.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: Two opposing arrows warn that you are leaving a one-way roadway and will meet oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: A stop sign is ahead; be prepared to stop
questions.explain: A Stop Ahead warning sign tells you to prepare to stop at a STOP sign ahead.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: A side road joins from the right
The road ends ahead; you must turn left or right
questions.explain: A T-intersection sign means the road you are on ends and you must turn.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road curves to the right ahead
questions.explain: This warning sign shows a curve to the right; reduce speed before entering it.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: This plaque below a curve warning sign shows:
options: A recommended safe speed for the curve
questions.explain: A yellow speed plaque gives an advisory speed for the hazard; under the Basic Speed Law you may need to go slower.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: A vehicle displaying this emblem is:
options: A slow-moving vehicle, usually traveling 25 mph or less
questions.explain: The orange-and-red triangle marks slow-moving vehicles such as road maintenance vehicles, which usually go 25 mph or less.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Slow-moving Vehicles'

questions.q: This orange sign means:
options: Road work ahead; slow down and watch for workers and equipment
questions.explain: Orange signs mark construction and maintenance zones; slow down, leave extra space and expect sudden stops.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Road Workers and Work Zones' / 'Move Over and Slow Down'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Keep to the right of the island or obstruction
questions.explain: A Keep Right sign directs you to pass to the right of a divider or obstruction.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Passing other vehicles is not allowed here
questions.explain: A DO NOT PASS sign prohibits passing in that section of road.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Signs'

questions.q: At an intersection with this sign and a green light, when you turn left you must:
options: Yield to oncoming traffic before turning
Turn only from the right lane
Turn first; oncoming traffic must stop
questions.explain: On a solid green light without an arrow your left turn is not protected; yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: Slow down and continue without stopping
The signal is broken; drive through
Stop and wait for a green light
Stop; after stopping, go when it is safe
questions.explain: A flashing red light means STOP; once stopped, you may proceed when it is safe.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: The light is about to turn green
Slow down and proceed with caution; you do not need to stop
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light is a warning: slow down, be alert, and proceed without stopping.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this light as you approach the intersection?
options: Always stop immediately, even if it is unsafe
Speed up to beat the red light
Proceed; yellow means the same as green
Stop if you can do so safely; otherwise cross with caution
questions.explain: A solid yellow light warns the signal is about to turn red; stop if you can safely, otherwise proceed cautiously.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: At this light, unless a sign prohibits it, you may:
options: Turn right after a complete stop when it is safe
questions.explain: A solid red light means stop, but you may turn right after stopping and yielding unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: This signal is green as you approach. What must you still do?
options: Yield to vehicles, bicyclists and pedestrians still in the intersection
questions.explain: On green you may go, but must yield to anyone still in the intersection and not enter if you cannot get completely across.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: You may turn left; oncoming traffic is stopped
Yield to oncoming traffic before turning left
questions.explain: A green arrow allows a protected turn in the direction shown while conflicting traffic is held by a red light.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: What does a solid red arrow mean?
options: Do not turn in that direction; stay stopped until a green light or arrow appears
The turn lane is closed permanently
questions.explain: You may not turn on a red arrow, even right; wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: What does a flashing yellow left-turn arrow mean?
options: Stop and wait for a solid green arrow
You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
questions.explain: A flashing yellow arrow permits an unprotected turn; you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: You approach an intersection where the traffic lights are not working. What should you do?
options: Stop as if there were stop signs in all directions, then proceed when safe
Slow down and proceed without stopping
Wait until the lights are repaired
questions.explain: When a signal is out, treat the intersection as an all-way stop.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Signals'

questions.q: The pedestrian signal is flashing DON'T WALK (raised hand) and a pedestrian is still in the crosswalk. You should:
options: Yield to the pedestrian until they finish crossing
Proceed, since the pedestrian should not be there
questions.explain: Drivers must yield to pedestrians even when the DON'T WALK signal is flashing.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Pedestrian Signals or Signs'

questions.q: What do these center lines mean for drivers?
options: No passing; you may cross them to turn left into a driveway or make a legal U-turn
questions.explain: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; a single set may be crossed to turn left into a driveway/private road or for a U-turn.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Lane Markings'

questions.q: These center lines are next to your lane. What do they allow?
questions.explain: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass if it is safe.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Lane Markings'

questions.q: What is the lane marked by these lines used for?
options: Preparing for and making left turns or U-turns from either direction
questions.explain: A two-way center left turn lane is only for starting left turns or U-turns, not for passing or regular travel.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Types of Lanes'

questions.q: What do double solid white lines mean?
options: You may change lanes with caution
Do not change lanes across them
questions.explain: Double solid white lines are a barrier (often for HOV lanes or ramps); never cross them to change lanes.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Lane Markings'

questions.q: Two sets of double solid yellow lines spaced two or more feet apart should be treated as:
options: A barrier you may not drive over or turn across
questions.explain: Two sets of double yellow lines 2+ feet apart form a barrier; do not cross them except at designated openings.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Lane Markings'

questions.q: A single solid yellow line on the center of a two-lane road with one lane in your direction means:
questions.explain: Do not pass when there is one lane your way and a solid yellow line on your side.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Lane Markings'

questions.q: A diamond-shaped placard on the back of a truck means the truck:
options: May be carrying a hazardous load
questions.explain: Diamond-shaped placards identify hazardous loads; such vehicles must stop before railroad tracks.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Vehicles with Hazardous Loads'

questions.q: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you and another vehicle arrive at the same time. Who goes first?
questions.explain: When two arrive together at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle, bicyclist or pedestrian on your right.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First?'

questions.q: At an uncontrolled intersection, which driver normally has the right-of-way?
options: The one on the wider road
The one going straight, regardless of arrival
questions.explain: The vehicle that reaches the intersection first has the right-of-way.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First?'

questions.q: At a T intersection with no STOP or YIELD signs, who has the right-of-way?
options: Traffic on the road that ends
questions.explain: Vehicles, bicyclists and pedestrians on the through road have the right-of-way at an uncontrolled T intersection.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First?'

questions.q: At a four-way stop, after you have stopped, how is the right-of-way decided?
options: Drivers going straight always go first
The first to stop goes first; if two arrive together, yield to the one on the right
questions.explain: At an all-way stop, stop first and then apply the arrival-order and yield-to-the-right rules.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First?'

questions.q: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to:
options: Pedestrians and oncoming vehicles close enough to be dangerous
No one if you signaled first
questions.explain: Left-turning drivers must yield to pedestrians and to approaching vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First?'

questions.q: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in:
questions.explain: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at marked or unmarked crosswalks.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Pedestrians' / 'Crosswalks'

questions.q: There is a limit line before a crosswalk where a pedestrian is crossing. Where should you stop?
options: Anywhere, as long as you slow down
questions.explain: Stop at the limit line in front of the crosswalk and wait for pedestrians to finish crossing.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Pedestrians' / 'Crosswalks'

questions.q: A pedestrian who is using a white cane or guide dog is waiting to cross. They:
options: Have the right-of-way at all times
Have the right-of-way only in marked crosswalks
Must wait for a gap in traffic
Should be warned with your horn
questions.explain: Blind pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes always have the right-of-way; never honk at them.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Pedestrians Who Are Blind'

questions.q: A blind pedestrian at a corner pulls in their cane and steps back from the curb. This usually means:
options: You must wait for them to cross
questions.explain: Pulling in the cane and stepping away from the intersection usually signals that the driver may proceed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Pedestrians Who Are Blind'

questions.q: A vehicle in the lane next to you is stopped at a crosswalk. What should you do?
options: Pass it carefully at reduced speed
Change lanes behind it and continue
Do not pass it; a pedestrian may be crossing out of view
questions.explain: A car stopped at a crosswalk may be hiding a pedestrian from your view, so never go around it.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Pedestrians' / 'Crosswalks'

questions.q: Which of these is considered a pedestrian?
options: A person driving a golf cart
questions.explain: Pedestrians include people on foot and people using roller skates, skateboards, or a wheelchair, tricycle or quadricycle due to a disability.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Pedestrians' / 'Crosswalks'

questions.q: When entering a roundabout, you must:
options: Yield only to vehicles on your right
Yield to all traffic already in the roundabout
Stop and wait for a signal
Enter first if you are going straight
questions.explain: Slow down and yield to everyone already circulating before entering.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: Which direction do you travel in a California roundabout?
options: Whichever direction is shortest to your exit
questions.explain: Traffic moves counterclockwise around the central island.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: You miss your exit in a roundabout. What should you do?
options: Exit at the next street and make a U-turn
Keep going around until you return to your exit
questions.explain: If you miss the exit, continue around the roundabout again.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: In a multi-lane roundabout, to turn right you should:
options: Use the right lane and exit in the right lane
Use either lane and change lanes inside
questions.explain: For a right turn, choose the right lane and exit in the right lane.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: Two vehicles meet on a steep, narrow mountain road where neither can pass. Who has the right-of-way?
questions.explain: The uphill-facing vehicle has the right-of-way; the downhill vehicle backs up because it has more control.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Mountain Roads'

questions.q: When merging onto a highway from an on-ramp, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explain: Highway traffic has the right-of-way; merge into a gap at or near traffic speed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Merging And Exiting'

questions.q: When pulling out of a driveway or parking space into traffic, you must:
options: Yield to traffic already in the lanes
Expect traffic to let you in
questions.explain: Vehicles entering traffic must proceed with caution and yield to traffic already occupying the lanes.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First?'

questions.q: Your light is green, but traffic is backed up on the far side of the intersection. You should:
options: Wait until there is room to get completely across
Turn on your hazard lights and proceed
Enter and wait in the intersection
questions.explain: It is illegal to enter and block an intersection when you cannot get completely across before the light turns red.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First?'

questions.q: An emergency vehicle with siren and red lights approaches from behind. What must you do?
options: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
questions.explain: Yield by pulling to the right edge and stopping until emergency vehicles have passed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: You are in the middle of an intersection when an emergency vehicle with a siren approaches. You should:
options: Turn left to get out of the way
Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop
Back up out of the intersection
questions.explain: Do not stop in the intersection; clear it, then move right and stop.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: A funeral procession led by a traffic officer is passing through an intersection. You should:
options: Join the line to get through faster
Let the procession pass; it has the right-of-way
questions.explain: Funeral processions have the right-of-way; interrupting one can result in a ticket.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Other Important Roadway Information'

questions.q: You want to turn left and an oncoming car has its right turn signal on. You should:
options: Wait until the car actually begins its turn before you go
Turn immediately, since it will turn before reaching you
questions.explain: Do not assume the signal is accurate; wait for the vehicle to start its turn.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Crossing or Entering Traffic'

questions.q: Before turning left from a two-way center left turn lane, you must respect the right-of-way of:
options: No one; the lane is yours once you enter
Any vehicle, bicyclist or motorcyclist already in that lane
questions.explain: When entering the center turn lane, yield to vehicles, bicyclists and motorcyclists already using it.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Left Turns'

questions.q: You are making a right turn on a green light. Who has the right-of-way in the crosswalk you are turning across?
options: You, because your light is green
Only pedestrians with a WALK signal at night
questions.explain: On a green light pedestrians still have the right-of-way; check for them and for bicycles beside you.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Right-of-Way Rules: Who Goes First?'

questions.q: You are in a dedicated right-turn lane that does not merge into another lane. The light for straight traffic is red. You may:
options: Turn without stopping, unless a light or sign on the right curb controls the lane, while yielding to pedestrians
Never turn until the light is green
Turn only after a full stop and waiting 5 seconds
questions.explain: A dedicated right-turn lane allows a turn even when through traffic has a red light, but obey any signal or sign for that lane and yield to pedestrians.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Right Turns'

questions.q: Who must yield when a light rail vehicle is approaching and you want to turn across its tracks?
options: You may turn if you signal
You must not turn in front of the approaching light rail vehicle
The light rail vehicle must stop for you
questions.explain: Never turn in front of an approaching light rail vehicle; turn across tracks only when the signal allows.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Buses, Streetcars, Trolleys' / 'Light Rail Vehicles'

questions.q: California's Basic Speed Law says you may never drive:
options: Faster than is safe for current conditions
Faster than 65 mph under any conditions
questions.explain: The Basic Speed Law prohibits driving faster than is safe for the conditions, regardless of the posted limit.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Manage Your Speed'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed limit on most California highways is:
questions.explain: Unless posted otherwise, the maximum on most California highways is 65 mph.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Manage Your Speed'

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, the maximum speed on a two-lane undivided highway is:
questions.explain: Two-lane undivided highways have a 55 mph limit unless otherwise posted.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Manage Your Speed'

questions.q: What is the maximum speed when towing a trailer in California?
questions.explain: Vehicles towing trailers are limited to 55 mph.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Manage Your Speed'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in a business or residential district is:
questions.explain: Business and residential districts are 25 mph unless signs say otherwise.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Business or Residential Districts'

questions.q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit within 500 feet of a school while children are outside or crossing?
questions.explain: The limit is 25 mph within 500 feet of a school when children are present; some school zones are posted as low as 15 mph.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Around Children'

questions.q: The 25 mph school-zone limit (when children are outside or crossing) starts how far from the school?
questions.explain: The school-zone limit applies within 500 feet of a school while children are present.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Around Children'

questions.q: What is the speed limit at a blind intersection (no stop signs at any corner and your view is blocked)?
questions.explain: Blind intersections have a 15 mph limit.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Blind Intersections' / 'Alleys'

questions.q: What is the speed limit in an alley?
questions.explain: Alleys have a 15 mph speed limit.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Blind Intersections' / 'Alleys'

questions.q: Within 100 feet of a railroad crossing where you cannot see the tracks for 400 feet in both directions, the speed limit is:
questions.explain: The limit is 15 mph unless the crossing is controlled by gates, a warning signal or a flagger.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Near Railroad or Light Rail Tracks'

questions.q: A streetcar is stopped at a safety zone. If you pass it, your speed may be no more than:
questions.explain: You may pass a bus, streetcar or trolley stopped at a safety zone or light at no more than 10 mph.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Buses, Streetcars, Trolleys' / 'Light Rail Vehicles'

questions.q: In heavy rain or snow you cannot see farther than 100 feet ahead. What is the fastest safe speed?
questions.explain: Once visibility drops to 100 feet or less, going over 30 mph is unsafe.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Slippery Roads'

questions.q: On a wet road, you should reduce your speed by about:
questions.explain: Slow down 5–10 mph on wet roads.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Slippery Roads'

questions.q: On packed snow, you should reduce your speed by:
questions.explain: Reduce your speed by half on packed snow.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Slippery Roads'

questions.q: On ice, you should drive no faster than:
questions.explain: On ice, slow to no more than 5 mph.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Slippery Roads'

questions.q: What following distance does the California handbook recommend in normal conditions?
questions.explain: Use the three-second rule to keep a safe following distance.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Tailgating (Following Too Closely)'

questions.q: How do you check that you are following at a safe distance?
options: When the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point, count; you should not reach that point before three seconds
Match the speed of the car ahead
Keep one car length per 20 mph
Stay close enough to see the driver's mirrors
questions.explain: Count seconds after the car ahead passes a landmark; reaching it before three seconds means you are too close.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 14, 'Glossary'

questions.q: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?
options: Keep your course and speed, then move right when safe to let them pass
questions.explain: Maintain course and speed, increase space ahead, and change lanes to the right when safe so the tailgater can pass.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Tailgating (Following Too Closely)'

questions.q: You should allow extra following distance behind a motorcycle when it is riding on:
options: Metal bridge gratings, railroad tracks or gravel
questions.explain: Give more space to motorcyclists on metal surfaces and gravel, where they can lose traction.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Tailgating (Following Too Closely)'

questions.q: How far ahead should you scan the road while driving?
options: Only to the car in front
questions.explain: Keep your eyes moving and look at least 10 seconds ahead to have time to react.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Be Aware of Your Surroundings'

questions.q: If you choose to drive slower than other traffic on a multilane road, you should:
questions.explain: Slower drivers should keep to the right lane; driving too slowly can also be cited.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Heavy Traffic or Bad Weather' / 'Towing'

questions.q: At 55 mph, a passenger car can stop in about 300 feet. A large truck at the same speed may need up to:
questions.explain: Large vehicles may need up to 400 feet to stop from 55 mph, more when heavily loaded.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Sharing the Road: Blind Spots (the No Zone)'

questions.q: To merge into or cross traffic on a city street, you need a gap of about:
questions.explain: On city streets you need about half a block (≈150 feet); on highways about a full block (≈300 feet).
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Crossing or Entering Traffic'

questions.q: To merge into traffic on a highway, you need a gap of about:
questions.explain: On a highway you need about a full block, roughly 300 feet.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Crossing or Entering Traffic'

questions.q: Neighborhood electric vehicles (NEVs) and low-speed vehicles may only use roads whose speed limit is no higher than:
questions.explain: NEVs and LSVs top out at 25 mph and are restricted from roads with limits above 35 mph.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Slow-moving Vehicles'

questions.q: A yellow advisory speed sign posted at a curve shows 35 mph and it is raining heavily. You should:
options: Drive slower than 35 mph if needed for safety
Drive 40 mph since it is only advisory
questions.explain: Under the Basic Speed Law, your speed must fit the conditions, which can mean going slower than the advisory speed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Manage Your Speed'

questions.q: How far before a turn should you begin signaling?
options: Just as you begin the turn
questions.explain: Signal at least 100 feet before turning.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Signaling'

questions.q: Before changing lanes on a freeway, you should signal for at least:
questions.explain: On a freeway, signal at least five seconds before a lane change.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Signaling'

questions.q: When exiting a highway from the proper lane, signal about:
options: Only after you are on the ramp
questions.explain: Signal about five seconds, roughly 400 feet, before you exit.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Merging And Exiting'

questions.q: On a California freeway, which lane is the 'Number 1 Lane'?
questions.explain: Lanes are numbered from the left; the leftmost lane is the Number 1 Lane.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Choosing a Lane' / 'Changing Lanes'

questions.q: Before changing lanes, you should check your blind spot by:
options: Looking over your shoulder in the direction you are moving
questions.explain: Signal, check mirrors, then look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Choosing a Lane' / 'Changing Lanes'

questions.q: When preparing for a right turn on a street with a bike lane, you may enter the bike lane:
options: Within 200 feet of the turn, after checking for bicyclists
At any distance before the turn
questions.explain: You may drive in a bike lane within 200 feet of the turn, after checking your blind spots for bicyclists.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Right Turns'

questions.q: When making a right turn, you should finish the turn:
options: In the right lane, without swinging wide
In the lane farthest from the curb
questions.explain: Begin and end a right turn in the lane closest to the right edge; do not swing wide.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Right Turns'

questions.q: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn right on a solid red light:
options: Only if a green arrow is also showing
Without stopping if the road is clear
After a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and traffic
questions.explain: Right turns on red are allowed after a full stop unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Right Turns'

questions.q: Can you turn right on a red arrow?
options: No; wait for a green light or arrow
Yes, if no pedestrians are present
questions.explain: You may not turn right while stopped at a red arrow.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Right Turns'

questions.q: You may turn left on a red light only when:
options: You are in a hurry for an emergency
Turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping, if no sign prohibits it
questions.explain: A left on red is legal only from a one-way street onto a one-way street, after stopping and yielding.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Left Turns'

questions.q: While waiting to turn left, why should you keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead?
options: If hit from behind, you won't be pushed into oncoming traffic
It is required only in roundabouts
questions.explain: Wheels turned left could send you into oncoming traffic if you are rear-ended.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Turns: Left Turns'

questions.q: When turning left from a two-way street onto another two-way street, you should end the turn in:
options: The left lane closest to the center of the street going your way
questions.explain: To reduce collision risk, finish in the left-most lane for your direction.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Examples of Turns'

questions.q: What is the longest distance you may drive in a two-way center left turn lane?
questions.explain: You may only drive up to 200 feet in the center left turn lane.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Types of Lanes'

questions.q: In a residential district, a U-turn is legal if:
options: No vehicles are approaching within 200 feet
You are on a one-way street
You use a fire station driveway
questions.explain: Residential U-turns are allowed when no vehicle is approaching within 200 feet.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'U-Turn'

questions.q: Where is a U-turn never allowed?
options: Across a single set of double yellow lines
At an intersection on a green light with no prohibiting sign
Through an opening in a divided highway
In front of a fire station
questions.explain: U-turns are prohibited in front of fire stations; never use a fire station driveway to turn around.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'U-Turn'

questions.q: To make a U-turn, how far must you be able to see clearly in each direction?
questions.explain: Do not make a U-turn when you cannot see clearly 200 feet each way.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'U-Turn'

questions.q: In a business district, U-turns are generally allowed only:
options: At an intersection, or at a divider opening on a divided highway
questions.explain: In business districts, U-turns are allowed only at intersections or at openings on divided highways (unless a sign prohibits).
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'U-Turn'

questions.q: When may you pass another vehicle on the right?
options: On a two-lane road using the shoulder
Anytime there is a paved shoulder
On a road with two or more lanes in your direction, when it is safe
Whenever the driver ahead is slow
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed on multi-lane roads, on one-way streets, or when the driver ahead is turning left and it is safe.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Passing'

questions.q: The driver ahead is signaling a left turn. You may pass:
options: By driving off the pavement on the right
On the right, if it is safe and you stay on the pavement
questions.explain: Never pass on the left of a driver signaling a left turn; you may pass on the right if safe.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Passing'

questions.q: What is the closest you may be to an intersection, bridge, tunnel or railroad crossing when passing another vehicle?
questions.explain: Passing is not allowed once you are 100 feet or closer to an intersection, bridge, tunnel, railroad crossing or similar hazard.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Passing'

questions.q: To safely pass on a two-lane road, a hill or curve ahead should be at least:
options: Just beyond the vehicle you are passing
questions.explain: Before passing, make sure any hill or curve is at least a third of a mile away.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Passing'

questions.q: Another driver signals that they want to pass you. You should:
options: Stay in your lane and keep a steady speed
questions.explain: Allow the pass by maintaining your lane position and speed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Passing'

questions.q: You are driving slowly on a two-lane road where passing is unsafe. What is the smallest number of vehicles behind you that requires you to pull into a turnout?
questions.explain: You must pull into a turnout when five or more vehicles are following you.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Types of Lanes'

questions.q: How should you enter or exit a carpool (HOV) lane separated by double solid lines?
options: Only at designated openings, not across the double lines
questions.explain: Do not cross double solid lines to enter or leave an HOV lane; use the designated entrances and exits.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Types of Lanes'

questions.q: You need to cross several lanes to reach your freeway exit. You should:
options: Signal and cross the lanes one at a time, checking blind spots each time
Stop in the lane until a gap opens
questions.explain: Change lanes one at a time, signaling and checking blind spots for each lane.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Merging And Exiting'

questions.q: When towing a trailer on a road with no marked slow lane and four or more lanes in your direction, you may use:
options: Only the two lanes closest to the right edge
questions.explain: Towing vehicles must use the right lane or slow-vehicle lane; with four or more lanes they may use the two right-most lanes.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Heavy Traffic or Bad Weather' / 'Towing'

questions.q: Which hand-and-arm signal means you plan to turn left?
options: Right arm straight out the passenger window
questions.explain: A left turn is signaled with the arm extended straight out the window.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Signaling'

questions.q: Which hand-and-arm signal means a right turn?
questions.explain: A right turn is signaled with the left arm bent up at the elbow.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Signaling'

questions.q: You plan to turn right just after crossing an intersection. When should you signal?
options: When you are almost through the intersection
questions.explain: Signaling early could make drivers think you will turn at the intersection; signal when almost through it.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Signaling'

questions.q: After parallel parking, what is the maximum distance your wheels may be from the curb?
questions.explain: Your vehicle should end up parallel and within 18 inches of the curb.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parallel Parking'

questions.q: How long should a parallel parking space be?
options: At least 3 feet longer than your vehicle
At least 10 feet longer than your vehicle
Exactly the length of your vehicle
Twice the length of your vehicle
questions.explain: Choose a gap that is at least three feet longer than your car.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parallel Parking'

questions.q: What is the closest you may legally park to a fire hydrant?
questions.explain: Keep at least 15 feet between your parked car and a fire hydrant or the driveway of a fire station.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Illegal Parking'

questions.q: With no curb extension, what is the closest you may park to a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
questions.explain: Parking is prohibited within 20 feet of a crosswalk, or 15 feet where a curb extension is present.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Illegal Parking'

questions.q: Where a crosswalk has a curb extension, what is the closest you may park to it?
questions.explain: With a curb extension, the no-parking distance from the crosswalk is 15 feet.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Illegal Parking'

questions.q: What is the closest you may park to a sidewalk ramp for disabled persons?
questions.explain: You must leave at least three feet between your vehicle and a wheelchair-access sidewalk ramp.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Illegal Parking'

questions.q: When parking downhill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
options: Toward the center of the road
questions.explain: Downhill: turn wheels into the curb so the car rolls into it if the brakes fail.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parking on a Hill'

questions.q: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
options: Away from the curb and let the car roll back gently against it
questions.explain: Uphill with a curb: turn wheels away from the curb and let the tire gently touch it.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parking on a Hill'

questions.q: When parking on a hill with no curb, turn your front wheels:
options: Toward the center of the road
Left if uphill, right if downhill
Toward the shoulder (right), so the car rolls away from traffic
questions.explain: With no curb, turn wheels right so the vehicle rolls away from the center of the road.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parking on a Hill'

questions.q: What does a white painted curb mean?
options: Stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers
questions.explain: White curbs are for brief passenger pickup and drop-off.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parking at Colored Curbs'

questions.q: What does a green painted curb mean?
options: Parking is allowed for a limited time
questions.explain: Green curbs allow limited-time parking; the limit is posted or painted.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parking at Colored Curbs'

questions.q: What does a yellow painted curb mean?
options: Stop only to load or unload passengers or freight, for no longer than posted
questions.explain: Yellow curbs are loading zones with a posted time limit; noncommercial drivers usually must stay with the vehicle.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parking at Colored Curbs'

questions.q: What does a red painted curb mean?
questions.explain: Red curbs mean no stopping, standing or parking (buses may stop in a bus-only red zone).
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parking at Colored Curbs'

questions.q: What does a blue painted curb mean?
options: Parking only for a disabled person or a driver transporting one, with a placard or special plate
questions.explain: Blue curbs are reserved for disabled parking with a placard or special license plate.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Parking at Colored Curbs'

questions.q: May you park in the crosshatched (diagonal-line) area beside a disabled parking space?
options: Yes, if you have a passenger
questions.explain: Parking in the crosshatched area next to a disabled space is illegal.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Illegal Parking'

questions.q: After how long may a vehicle stopped, parked or left standing on a freeway be removed?
questions.explain: Vehicles left on a freeway longer than four hours may be removed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Illegal Parking'

questions.q: Which is a legal place to park, if no signs prohibit it?
options: At a curb more than 20 feet from a crosswalk
Between a safety zone and the curb
questions.explain: A curb more than 20 feet from a crosswalk can be legal if nothing else forbids it; sidewalks, double parking and the space between a safety zone and the curb are always illegal.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Illegal Parking'

questions.q: When you pass a bicyclist and cannot change lanes, you must leave at least how much space?
questions.explain: California requires at least three feet between your vehicle and a bicyclist you are passing.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Passing a Bicyclist'

questions.q: You cannot give a bicyclist three feet of clearance to pass. What should you do?
options: Wait behind them until you can pass with three feet of clearance
questions.explain: If three feet is not possible, do not pass until it is.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Passing a Bicyclist'

questions.q: When is it legal for a car to drive in a bicycle lane?
options: Any time no bicyclists are present
When parking where allowed, entering or leaving the road, or turning within 200 feet of an intersection
questions.explain: Driving in a bike lane is illegal except to park, enter or leave the road, or turn within 200 feet of the intersection.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Bicycle Lanes'

questions.q: Which bicyclists are required to wear a helmet in California?
questions.explain: Bicyclists under 18 must wear a helmet.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Bicycles'

questions.q: A bicyclist moves left away from the right edge of the lane. This is legal when the bicyclist is:
options: Avoiding a hazard or preparing for a left turn
questions.explain: Bicyclists may leave the right edge to pass, prepare for a left turn, avoid hazards, or when the lane is too narrow to share.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Bicycles'

questions.q: You are driving behind a large truck and cannot see its side mirrors. This means:
options: The truck driver cannot see you
You are at a safe distance
questions.explain: If you can't see the truck's mirrors, you are in its No Zone and the driver can't see you.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Sharing the Road: Blind Spots (the No Zone)'

questions.q: A large truck ahead signals a right turn but swings left first. You should:
options: Honk and pass on the left
Pass it on the right quickly
Stay back and not try to squeeze past on the right
questions.explain: Trucks swing wide to turn; check their signals and don't move into the space they need.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Sharing the Road: Blind Spots (the No Zone)'

questions.q: Why is it dangerous to change lanes in front of a large truck and then slow down?
options: It is only dangerous at night
Trucks need much more distance to stop
Truck drivers can see too far ahead
questions.explain: Large vehicles take longer to stop, so cutting in and slowing can cause a crash.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Sharing the Road: Blind Spots (the No Zone)'

questions.q: When passing a large truck, you should:
options: Pass on the left and move ahead of it promptly
Stay beside it to be seen
questions.explain: Always pass large vehicles on the left and do not linger alongside them.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Sharing the Road: Blind Spots (the No Zone)'

questions.q: What following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle?
questions.explain: Allow a three-second following distance in case the rider brakes suddenly or falls.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Motorcycles'

questions.q: Is lane splitting by motorcycles legal in California?
questions.explain: Sharing lanes with motorcycles (lane splitting) is legal in California.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Motorcycles'

questions.q: Should you pass a motorcycle while sharing its lane?
options: No, never try to pass a motorcycle in the same lane
Yes, if the rider is slow
questions.explain: Give a motorcycle the full lane and never pass it within the same lane.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Motorcycles'

questions.q: Safety zones for bus or streetcar passengers are marked by raised buttons or markers. You may:
questions.explain: Safety zones are off-limits to vehicles in all circumstances.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Buses, Streetcars, Trolleys' / 'Light Rail Vehicles'

questions.q: Generally, may you pass a light rail vehicle or streetcar on its left side?
options: No, except in limited cases such as a one-way street or when an officer directs it
questions.explain: Passing a streetcar or light rail vehicle on the left is not allowed unless the tracks prevent passing on the right, on a one-way street, or when directed by an officer.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Buses, Streetcars, Trolleys' / 'Light Rail Vehicles'

questions.q: A school bus ahead is flashing red lights. What must you do?
options: Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully
Stop, then pass when no children are visible
Stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing
questions.explain: You must stop from either direction and stay stopped while the red lights flash.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Around Children'

questions.q: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on the other side of a highway that has two or more lanes in each direction. You:
options: Must stop only during school hours
questions.explain: On a divided or multilane highway (two or more lanes each way), traffic on the opposite side need not stop.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Around Children'

questions.q: A school bus is flashing yellow lights. This means:
options: The bus is preparing to stop; slow down and prepare to stop
You may pass at normal speed
The bus is letting children off now
questions.explain: Flashing yellow lights warn that the bus is about to stop; slow down and be prepared.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Around Children'

questions.q: Failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights can result in:
options: A fine of up to $1,000 and a 1-year suspension of your driving privilege
questions.explain: The penalty can be up to $1,000 and a one-year suspension.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Around Children'

questions.q: You approach a stopped tow truck on the shoulder displaying flashing amber lights. You must:
questions.explain: California's Move Over and Slow Down law covers stationary emergency vehicles, tow trucks and road work vehicles with warning lights.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Road Workers and Work Zones' / 'Move Over and Slow Down'

questions.q: Traffic fines in a highway construction or maintenance zone are doubled when:
questions.explain: Fines double in construction or maintenance zones when workers are present.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Road Workers and Work Zones' / 'Move Over and Slow Down'

questions.q: Assaulting a highway worker can bring a fine of up to:
options: $2,000 and up to 1 year in jail
questions.explain: Assaulting a highway worker is punishable by up to $2,000 and up to one year of imprisonment.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Road Workers and Work Zones' / 'Move Over and Slow Down'

questions.q: When driving through a work zone, you should:
options: Follow closely to keep traffic moving
Slow down, leave extra space and expect sudden stops
Speed up to clear it quickly
questions.explain: In work zones slow down, increase following distance, avoid distractions and obey flaggers.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Road Workers and Work Zones' / 'Move Over and Slow Down'

questions.q: At night, a vehicle with only one light is coming toward you. You should:
options: Move as far right as possible; it could be a bicycle, motorcycle or car with a missing headlight
questions.explain: A single light could be a bicycle, motorcycle or a car with a burned-out headlight; give it room.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Darkness'

questions.q: Why must you be especially careful around blind pedestrians when driving a hybrid or electric vehicle?
options: These vehicles are quiet and blind pedestrians rely on sound
questions.explain: Blind pedestrians rely on sound, and quiet vehicles may not be heard.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Pedestrians Who Are Blind'

questions.q: On a two-lane road, an oncoming car approaches while a bicyclist is ahead on your right. What should you do?
options: Squeeze between the car and the bicyclist
Speed up to pass both at once
Slow down, let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist with plenty of room
questions.explain: Take one danger at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then move left to give the bicyclist at least three feet.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Choose Between Hazards'

questions.q: When a fire engine, ambulance or police vehicle has its siren or flashing lights on, how far behind it must you stay at a minimum?
questions.explain: Do not follow within 300 feet of an emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: What can happen if you drive to the scene of a fire or collision just to look?
questions.explain: Driving to a disaster scene can get in the way of emergency crews and can result in arrest.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: For hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering, where should your hands be on the wheel?
options: At 9 and 3 o'clock or 8 and 4 o'clock
questions.explain: Push/pull steering starts with hands at 9 and 3 or 8 and 4 without crossing over the middle.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Controlling the Vehicle'

questions.q: When is hand-over-hand steering recommended?
options: Turning at low speeds, parking, or recovering from a skid
questions.explain: Hand-over-hand steering is for low-speed turns, parking and skid recovery.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Controlling the Vehicle'

questions.q: Is it legal to wear a headset or earplugs in both ears while driving?
questions.explain: Wearing a headset or earplugs in both ears while driving is illegal.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'An Introduction to Driving'

questions.q: An oncoming vehicle is approaching at night. At what distance does the requirement to switch to low beams begin?
questions.explain: Switch to low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Using Your Headlights'

questions.q: You are following another vehicle at night. At what distance behind it does the requirement to use low beams begin?
questions.explain: Use low beams within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Using Your Headlights'

questions.q: When must your headlights be on?
options: From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
From sunset to sunrise only on freeways
questions.explain: Headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and in other low-visibility conditions.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Using Your Headlights'

questions.q: If you need to use your windshield wipers because of rain, fog or snow, you must also:
options: Turn on only your parking lights
questions.explain: California requires low-beam headlights whenever weather requires the use of windshield wipers.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Using Your Headlights'

questions.q: An oncoming driver's headlights are blinding you. You should:
options: Look toward the right edge of your lane
questions.explain: Avoid looking into the lights; watch the right edge of your lane and the vehicle out of the corner of your eye.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Darkness'

questions.q: In heavy fog, you should use:
questions.explain: High beams reflect off fog; use low beams and never drive with only parking or fog lights.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Fog or Heavy Smoke'

questions.q: Your car begins to skid on a slippery road. What should you do first?
options: Ease off the accelerator, don't brake, and steer in the direction of the skid
questions.explain: Slowly remove your foot from the gas, avoid the brakes, and turn the wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Skids'

questions.q: In a locked-wheel skid in a vehicle with four-wheel antilock brakes (ABS), you should:
options: Apply firm pressure on the brake pedal
questions.explain: With four-wheel ABS, keep firm pressure on the brake pedal.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Skids'

questions.q: Your vehicle starts to hydroplane. You should:
options: Slow down gradually and avoid using the brakes
questions.explain: Sudden braking during hydroplaning may cause loss of control; ease off and slow gradually.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Hydroplaning'

questions.q: When is the road often most slippery?
options: Right after the road is swept
When it first starts to rain after a dry period
questions.explain: Oil and dust that haven't been washed away make pavement very slippery when rain starts.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Slippery Roads'

questions.q: Which part of the road tends to freeze first in cold weather?
questions.explain: Bridges and overpasses freeze before the rest of the road; shady areas also freeze first and dry last.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Slippery Roads'

questions.q: Who is responsible for a passenger under 16 not wearing a seat belt?
options: Only the passenger's parent if present
questions.explain: You can get a ticket if a passenger under 16 is not buckled.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Seat Belts'

questions.q: A child under 2 years old who weighs under 40 pounds and is under 3 feet 4 inches tall must ride in:
options: The front seat on a lap
questions.explain: These young children must ride in a rear-facing child restraint.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Child Restraint System and Safety Seats'

questions.q: Children under 8 years old or shorter than 4 feet 9 inches must generally be secured in:
options: A rear seat with no restraint
Any seat with a lap belt only
A child passenger restraint system in a rear seat
The front seat with a seat belt
questions.explain: Children under 8 or under 4'9" ride in a child restraint in the back seat, with limited exceptions.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Child Restraint System and Safety Seats'

questions.q: Where may a rear-facing child seat NOT be placed?
options: In the middle of the rear seat
In the front seat of a vehicle with an active passenger airbag
questions.explain: A rear-facing child restraint may not ride in front of an airbag.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Child Restraint System and Safety Seats'

questions.q: How far should you sit from the steering-wheel airbag cover?
options: At least 10 inches, measured from the wheel's center to your breastbone
questions.explain: Sit at least 10 inches from the airbag cover if you can still control the vehicle.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Air Bags' / 'Unattended Children and Pets'

questions.q: Under California law, a child may not be left unattended in a vehicle up to and including what age?
questions.explain: A child 6 or younger may not be left alone in a vehicle; supervision by someone at least 12 is allowed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Air Bags' / 'Unattended Children and Pets'

questions.q: Under California law, how may an adult driver use a cell phone while driving?
options: Only in hands-free mode, with a mounted phone and single swipe or tap
Any way, if using a headset in both ears
Holding it to talk if driving slowly
questions.explain: Adults may use a phone only hands-free; a mounted phone may be operated with a single swipe or touch.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Cell Phones and Texting' / 'Minors and Cell Phones'

questions.q: Can a driver under 18 use a hands-free cell phone while driving?
options: No, except to call for emergency help
questions.explain: Minors may not use a phone or wireless device while driving, even hands-free, except for emergency calls.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Cell Phones and Texting' / 'Minors and Cell Phones'

questions.q: Your phone rings while you are driving. The best action is to:
options: Answer quickly and keep it short
Hold it on speaker in your hand
Let it go to voicemail and pull off the road safely if you must call back
questions.explain: Do not answer while driving; pull over safely if you need to return the call.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Cell Phones and Texting' / 'Minors and Cell Phones'

questions.q: Which is a common symptom of carbon monoxide poisoning?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide symptoms include tiredness, yawning, dizziness, nausea, headache and ringing in the ears.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Be Aware of Carbon Monoxide'

questions.q: How do you check your blind spots?
options: Turn your head and look over your shoulder
questions.explain: Look over your shoulder through the side windows; turn only your head, not your body or the wheel.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Blind Spots'

questions.q: Cargo extends more than 4 feet past your rear bumper. During the day it must display:
