options: A 12-inch red or fluorescent orange square flag
questions.explain: Loads extending over 4 feet behind the bumper need a 12-inch red or fluorescent orange flag (two red lights at night).
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Other Important Roadway Information'

questions.q: May a person ride in the back of a pickup truck?
options: Only if the truck bed has secured seats and seat belts
questions.explain: No one may ride in the back of a pickup unless the vehicle has secure seats and seat belts there.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Other Important Roadway Information'

questions.q: On a narrow mountain road where you cannot see at least 200 feet ahead, you should:
options: Drive in the center of the road
Use your horn to alert oncoming traffic
questions.explain: Sound your horn on narrow mountain roads when you can't see 200 feet ahead.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Using Your Horn'

questions.q: Being pulled over by law enforcement, you should first:
options: Drive to the next exit before signaling
Get out and walk to the officer
Turn on your right signal and move completely onto the right shoulder
questions.explain: Signal right to acknowledge the officer and pull fully onto the right shoulder, even from the HOV lane.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 6, 'Law Enforcement Stops'

questions.q: When drivers are in fog or heavy smoke, which statement is true?
options: Use high beams to see farther
Increase following distance and be able to stop within the distance you can see
Pass slower vehicles to get out of the fog
questions.explain: Drive slowly, use low beams, increase following distance and avoid passing.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Fog or Heavy Smoke'

questions.q: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines:
options: Can impair your driving; you are responsible for knowing their effects
Are always safe if a doctor prescribed them
questions.explain: Many medicines cause drowsiness; drivers must know the effects of what they take.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'An Introduction to Driving'

questions.q: It is illegal for a driver 21 or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explain: Drivers 21 and over may not drive with a BAC of 0.08% or more.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) Limits'

questions.q: It is illegal for a driver under 21 to drive with a BAC of:
questions.explain: California has a 0.01% limit for drivers under 21.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) Limits'

questions.q: What is the BAC limit when driving a vehicle that requires a commercial driver's license?
questions.explain: Commercial drivers are prohibited from driving with a BAC of 0.04% or higher.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) Limits'

questions.q: What is the BAC limit for a driver transporting passengers for hire?
questions.explain: Driving a passenger for hire with a BAC of 0.04% or more is illegal.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) Limits'

questions.q: A driver of any age who is on DUI probation may not drive with a BAC of:
questions.explain: Drivers on DUI probation are subject to a 0.01% limit at any age.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) Limits'

questions.q: By driving in California, you have agreed to:
options: Take a drug test every year
Take a breath, blood or urine test if suspected of DUI
questions.explain: Under implied consent, drivers consent to chemical testing if lawfully suspected of DUI.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'DUI Arrests'

questions.q: If you refuse to take a required chemical test, the DMV will:
options: Suspend or revoke your driving privilege for 1 year
questions.explain: Refusing a chemical test results in a one-year suspension or revocation.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Alcohol and Drugs'

questions.q: When arrested for DUI, an officer may take your license and give you a temporary license valid for:
questions.explain: Under Administrative Per Se, the officer may issue a 30-day temporary license.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'DUI Arrests'

questions.q: After a DUI arrest, you may request a DMV administrative hearing within:
questions.explain: You have 10 days from the arrest date to request a DMV hearing.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'DUI Arrests'

questions.q: If convicted of DUI, the DMV will suspend or revoke your driving privilege and you must:
options: Complete a DUI program and file proof of insurance (SR 22/SR 1P)
questions.explain: A DUI conviction requires a DUI program, SR 22/SR 1P, reissue fees and possibly an ignition interlock device.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'DUI Convictions'

questions.q: How long does a DUI conviction remain on your driver record?
questions.explain: DUI convictions stay on your record for 10 years.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'DUI Convictions'

questions.q: A DUI conviction can lead to which of the following?
options: Jail time, fines and impoundment of your vehicle
questions.explain: Penalties can include up to six months in jail, fines and vehicle impoundment, plus civil lawsuits if someone is hurt.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'DUI Convictions'

questions.q: If you carry an opened container of alcohol in your car, where must it be kept?
options: In the trunk or an area where passengers do not sit
questions.explain: Open containers must be kept in the trunk or a non-passenger area; the glove box is not allowed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Use or Possession of Alcohol or Cannabis Products in a Vehicle'

questions.q: Can a passenger legally smoke or eat cannabis in a moving private car?
options: Yes, if it is medical cannabis
Yes, if the driver does not use it
questions.explain: No one may drink alcohol or smoke or eat cannabis while driving or riding as a passenger.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Use or Possession of Alcohol or Cannabis Products in a Vehicle'

questions.q: A driver under 21 may carry alcohol in a vehicle only if:
options: A person 21 or older is present and the container is full, sealed and unopened
It is in the glove box
It is beer or wine only
questions.explain: Under 21s may not carry alcohol unless accompanied by someone 21+ with a full, sealed container (with a narrow work exception).
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Drivers Under 21'

questions.q: A driver under 21 is caught with alcohol in the vehicle. The vehicle can be impounded for up to:
questions.explain: Law enforcement can impound the vehicle for up to 30 days, and the court may suspend the license for one year.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Drivers Under 21'

questions.q: A driver under 21 takes a preliminary alcohol screening (PAS) test that shows a BAC of 0.05% or higher. What may happen?
options: The driver is warned and released automatically
The officer may require a breath or blood test and the driver may be arrested for DUI
questions.explain: A PAS of 0.05% or more may lead to a required breath or blood test and possible DUI arrest.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Drivers Under 21'

questions.q: Is it illegal to drive under the influence of a legally prescribed medication?
options: No, prescriptions are always legal to drive on
Yes, if it impairs your ability to drive safely
Only if you have no prescription label
questions.explain: The law does not distinguish between illegal drugs and medications when they impair driving.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Alcohol and Drugs'

questions.q: Can you be convicted of DUI with a BAC below the legal limit?
questions.explain: Depending on impairment, you may be arrested and convicted even without a BAC measurement or below the limit.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) Limits'

questions.q: Which of these equals one standard drink in the handbook's BAC table?
questions.explain: One drink is 12 oz of 5% beer, 5 oz of 12% wine, or 1.5 oz of 80-proof liquor.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) Limits'

questions.q: A person aged 13 to 20 is convicted of riding a bicycle under the influence. What can happen to their driving privilege?
options: It can be suspended or delayed for 1 year
questions.explain: Bicycle DUI at ages 13–20 can lead to a one-year suspension or delay once eligible to drive.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 9, 'Alcohol and Drugs'

questions.q: A person aged 15 to 20 is convicted of using alcohol or a controlled substance. The court will order the DMV to:
options: Suspend their driving privilege for 1 year or delay eligibility
questions.explain: The court orders a one-year suspension or a delay in license eligibility.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Maintaining Your Minor's (Provisional) Driver's License'

questions.q: Using a vehicle to flee from law enforcement is a misdemeanor punishable by:
options: Up to 1 year in county jail
questions.explain: Evading law enforcement is punishable by up to one year in county jail; more if someone is injured or killed.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Evading Law Enforcement'

questions.q: The DMV will revoke your driving privilege if you are convicted of:
options: Failing to renew registration on time
Hit-and-run or reckless driving that causes injury
questions.explain: Hit-and-run and reckless driving causing injury result in revocation.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Traffic Violator School' / 'Suspension or Revocation'

questions.q: You are involved in a collision. What must you do first?
options: Drive home and call your insurer
Stop only if there is major damage
Leave if it was not your fault
Stop; leaving the scene is a hit-and-run
questions.explain: You must stop at a collision; failing to do so is a hit-and-run with severe penalties.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'What to Do if You Are in a Collision'

questions.q: You must report a collision to the DMV (form SR 1) within 10 days if:
options: Property damage is over $5,000, and in no other case
Property damage is over $1,000 or anyone is injured or killed
Police were called to the scene
You were the driver at fault
questions.explain: An SR 1 is required within 10 days for over $1,000 damage or any injury or death.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'Reporting a Collision'

questions.q: Which statement about the SR 1 collision report is true?
options: Only the at-fault driver files it
It is not needed on private property
Each driver must file it, even if not at fault and even on private property
questions.explain: Every driver involved must file; law enforcement will not make the DMV report for you.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'Reporting a Collision'

questions.q: If anyone is injured or killed in a collision, you must report it to law enforcement within:
questions.explain: Injury or fatal collisions must be reported to law enforcement within 24 hours.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'What to Do if You Are in a Collision'

questions.q: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?
options: Leave a secure note with your name, phone number and address, and report it to law enforcement
Leave without a note if the damage is minor
Report it only to your insurer
Wait until the owner returns, however long it takes
questions.explain: Attach a note with your contact information and report the collision to law enforcement.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'What to Do if You Are in a Collision'

questions.q: California's minimum liability insurance must cover at least how much for injury or death of one person?
questions.explain: Minimum coverage is $30,000 for one person, $60,000 for more than one, and $15,000 for property damage.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'Insurance Requirements' / 'Driving Without Insurance'

questions.q: California's minimum liability insurance for property damage is:
questions.explain: Coverage must include at least $15,000 for property damage.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'Insurance Requirements' / 'Driving Without Insurance'

questions.q: Minimum liability coverage for injury or death of more than one person is:
questions.explain: The minimum is $60,000 for injury or death to more than one person.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'Insurance Requirements' / 'Driving Without Insurance'

questions.q: If you are in a collision without proper insurance, your license can be suspended for up to:
options: 1 year, only if you were at fault
4 years, no matter who was at fault
questions.explain: Driving uninsured and being in a collision can bring up to a four-year suspension regardless of fault.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'Insurance Requirements' / 'Driving Without Insurance'

questions.q: You have a tire blowout. What should you do?
options: Hold the wheel firmly, gradually release the accelerator, and slow down before pulling off
Swerve onto the shoulder at once
questions.explain: Avoid sudden braking; keep a firm grip, ease off the gas and steer to stabilize, then pull off when safe.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Tire Blowouts' / 'Driving Off the Pavement'

questions.q: Your right wheels drift off the pavement onto the shoulder. You should:
options: Grip the wheel, ease off the gas, brake gently, then steer back carefully
questions.explain: Remove your foot from the accelerator, brake gently, check traffic, then carefully steer back on.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Tire Blowouts' / 'Driving Off the Pavement'

questions.q: Your car breaks down on the freeway. After pulling onto the right shoulder, you should generally:
options: Walk along the freeway to find help
Leave the car in the traffic lane
Stand behind the car to wave down help
Stay in the vehicle with your seat belt on until help arrives
questions.explain: Exit and re-enter on the side away from traffic, and stay inside with your belt on unless it is safer to get out and away.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'If Your Vehicle Becomes Disabled on the Freeway'

questions.q: Your car stalls on railroad tracks and a train is coming. What should you do?
options: Get out immediately and run away from the tracks diagonally toward the direction the train is coming from
Stay in the car and call 911
Run away in the same direction the train is traveling
questions.explain: Leave the vehicle at once and move diagonally toward the oncoming train so you avoid flying debris, then call 911.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Disabled Vehicles on Railroad Tracks'

questions.q: Your car stalls on railroad tracks and no train is coming. You should:
options: Push the car to the next town
Get out and call the number posted at the crossing, then call 911
Wait in the car for the next train to pass
questions.explain: Exit and call the railroad emergency number on the crossing post or control box, giving the crossing number, then 911.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Disabled Vehicles on Railroad Tracks'

questions.q: When a train is approaching a crossing, you must stop at least how far from the nearest track?
questions.explain: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when warned of a train.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Near Railroad or Light Rail Tracks'

questions.q: Red lights are flashing at a railroad crossing and the gate rises. You should:
options: Cross as soon as the gate rises
Wait until the red lights stop flashing before crossing
questions.explain: Do not cross until the lights stop flashing, even if the gate goes up.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Near Railroad or Light Rail Tracks'

questions.q: The crossing gates are down but you see no train. You should:
options: Stay behind the gates and call the posted railroad number or 911
Back up and take the tracks at speed
questions.explain: Never go around or under lowered gates; call the posted number or 911 if no train comes.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 7, 'Near Railroad or Light Rail Tracks'

questions.q: You see a collision ahead. How can you warn drivers behind you?
options: Turn on emergency flashers or tap your brakes three or four times
questions.explain: Use flashers, lightly tap the brakes several times, or use a hand signal when slowing.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Using Your Emergency Flashers'

questions.q: If your car has trouble and you must stop, where should you avoid stopping?
options: Well off the road on a straight section
In a visible spot on the shoulder
Just over a hill or just around a curve
questions.explain: Other drivers may not see you in time if you stop just over a hill or around a curve.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 5, 'Using Your Emergency Flashers'

questions.q: An officer is conducting a traffic break, weaving across lanes with lights on. You should:
options: Turn on your flashers, slow gradually to the officer's speed, and not pass the patrol car
Exit the freeway on the shoulder
questions.explain: Slow down gradually, keep a safe distance and do not pass until the officer turns off the lights.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Law Enforcement Traffic Breaks'

questions.q: Your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor. First you should:
questions.explain: Quickly pump the brakes; if needed, downshift and use the parking/emergency brake.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 8, 'Skids'

questions.q: What should you do if anyone is hurt in a collision?
options: Drive the injured person to a hospital yourself
Wait for someone else to call
questions.explain: Call 911 immediately if anyone is injured.
questions.ref: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, rev. 6/2025), Section 10, 'What to Do if You Are in a Collision'
